about: Cathiard Vineyard is the Napa Valley estate of Florence and Daniel Cathiard, the owners of Château Smith Haut Lafitte in Bordeaux. In early 2020 they bought a historic property on the lower slopes of the Mayacamas Mountains, straddling the Rutherford and St. Helena appellations, from the Flora Springs families. The land was once part of Rancho Carne Humana, granted to Dr. Edward Bale in the 1840s. In 1887 the Scottish brothers James and William Rennie bought it, planted 60 acres and built a stone gravity-flow winery, before fire and phylloxera ended their venture.

Founding Brothers honours the Rennies, whose portraits appear on the label, and is the estate’s flagship red. It comes only from estate hillside vines, typically 20 to 30 years old. The 2021 is a blend led by Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot and a little Cabernet Franc; malolactic fermentation happens naturally in barrel, and the wine ages 16 to 18 months, mostly in medium-toast French oak, part new and part in large foudres. Winemaker Justine Labbé, with consultant Michel Rolland, aims for a Bordeaux-like finesse and freshness rather than the heaviest Napa style.

Critics have taken the comparison seriously: Jeb Dunnuck likened the 2021 to a Saint-Julien, with cassis, graphite and tobacco, while Decanter found red flowers, herbs, plum, cherry and pomegranate over very fine tannins, and Jancis Robinson called it distinctly Bordeaux-like. James Suckling noted flowers, currants and pine needles with ultra-fine tannins. Remarkably, 2021 was only the second vintage made under the Cathiard name, and it earned 95 points or more from five major critics.
facts: About 60% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 10% Cabernet Franc (2021)
Estate hillside vines, Rutherford and St. Helena, 20–30 years old
16–18 months in French oak, part new, part large foudres
